main_issue: Whether alcohol can be served at the housewarming in the flat, resolved by putting the drinks in a cooler outside the front door.

A-B.evidence: B said 'looks good' (T2) and A bought the drinks; both later accept the cooler outside (T17, T19). They never address each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C asked A about the cooler outside the door (T15) and A replied 'a cooler outside works for me' (T17).

A-D.evidence: A asked what D meant (T8); D said no alcohol at all (T9). D then accepted the cooler outside (T14) and A agreed (T17, T21).

B-C.evidence: C asked B whether the cooler works for the manager (T18) and B said 'that works for me' (T19).

B-D.evidence: B wanted drinks available for the manager (T10), D opposed alcohol (T9). D accepted the cooler outside (T14) and B accepted it (T19), though they never addressed each other.

C-D.evidence: C offered the kitchen (T11) and D declined (T12). C proposed the cooler outside (T13) and D said 'I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C' (T14).
